findings.title: Rejected device is cached as tagged, so a retry bypasses the limit
findings.body: tagDeviceUI calls localCache.SetDefault(key, ...) before anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, TagDevice/Authenticate deny that first request, but the device ID remains cached for the cache's 29-minute default lifetime. The next request hits the cache at line 83 and returns nil without touching the store, so Anonymous.Authenticate succeeds even though the device was never recorded and the limit is still reached. The limit therefore only denies the first attempt per device per instance; clients just retry to get in. The cache must only be populated after a successful store, and must be evicted on error.

findings.title: Device limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert and can be exceeded concurrently
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active devices and then, in a separate DB session, inserts a new device if count < deviceLimit. There is no transaction, lock, or unique constraint enforcement tying the count to the insert, so many concurrent first-time requests from different devices can all observe count == limit-1 and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. Under anonymous traffic (the exact load this feature limits) the cap is therefore not reliably enforced; enforcement needs to be serialized/atomic in the store.

findings.title: Provider signature changed without regenerating Wire injection
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB instead of anonstore.AnonStore, and ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an extra int64 argument, but no pkg/server/wire.go / wire_gen.go changes are included. Grafana builds from the checked-in generated wire_gen.go, which still constructs AnonDBStore with one argument and passes it to ProvideAnonymousDeviceService where a db.DB is now expected, so the server package will not compile / DI is stale until `make wire` (or equivalent) is run and the generated file committed.

findings.title: Tagging moved from async background work to the synchronous auth path
findings.body: Previously TagDevice ran in a goroutine with a 2-minute background-context timeout and panic recovery; now Authenticate blocks on TagDevice (a CountDevices query plus an insert/update on cache miss) using the request context. This adds database latency to anonymous authentication, makes auth fail/slow when the store is slow, ties DB writes to request-context cancellation, and removes the panic recovery around tagging. Combined with the per-instance 29-minute cache, cache misses across many instances will also amplify DB load. If synchronous enforcement is required, it needs a bounded timeout/context handling rather than the raw request context.

findings.title: Existing device inactive for >30 days is treated as over-limit instead of an existing device
findings.body: When count >= deviceLimit, updateDevice only updates rows whose updated_at is within the last 30 days (anonymousDeviceExpiration). Devices are only deleted after 61 days (keepFor in impl.go), so a known device returning after 30-61 days still exists in anon_device but its UPDATE matches 0 rows and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, denying a previously registered device. The stated intent ('if device limit is reached, only update devices') is not met for this window; existence should be checked separately from the 30-day activity window.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit contract mismatch: Go always sends 0, frontend type expects undefined for unset
findings.body: AnonymousDeviceLimit is a plain int64 without omitempty, so an unconfigured instance (limit 0 = unlimited in the backend) serializes as anonymousDeviceLimit: 0. The frontend declares it `number | undefined` and GrafanaBootConfig defaults it to undefined to mean unset. Consumers cannot distinguish 'unlimited/0' from an explicitly configured value via the declared type, and any frontend logic checking for undefined to mean 'no limit' will never see it from a real server. Use a pointer/omitempty or document 0 as the unlimited sentinel consistently.
